component.name: Kosmic PDF
component.summary: View, organise, annotate and redact PDFs

description.p: Kosmic PDF is a lightweight, free and open-source PDF viewer and editor, made by Kosmos for law practice.

ul.li: Reorder, rotate, copy and paste pages with drag and drop, including between files
Open several PDFs in tabs, and drag tabs into windows of their own
Highlight, type notes onto pages, and select and copy text
Redact text and areas permanently, and stamp Bates numbers
Place exhibit labels on pages, and label and renumber a set of exhibit files at once
Make scanned PDFs searchable with OCR, and convert to PDF/A
Combine files, turn images into PDFs, and flatten annotations

description.p: A Move tool (the hand) drags the page around in the window, and files now open with it chosen. Holding Space borrows it with any tool.
Brings the changes in 0.3.4 to Windows; nothing changes on Linux.
Label Exhibit Files now labels and renames the files themselves where they are, unless you choose labelled copies instead.
At its first start, Kosmic PDF shows its terms of use (no warranty; use at your own risk) and runs once they are accepted, on Linux as on Windows.
On Windows, the installer and the program's first start show the terms of use (no warranty; use at your own risk) and go on only once they are accepted.
Kosmic PDF now runs on Windows too: an installer, with OCR and PDF/A included, is at kosmos.law/pdf. Opening a PDF from the file manager still goes to the running window on every system.

Exhibit labels. The Exhibit Label tool (L) places a labelled sticker on the page: choose a caption such as "Plaintiff Exhibit", the number or letter, a pale background colour and a size, watch the label follow the pointer, and click to place it. Labels can be dragged to a new spot, edited with a double-click, and removed with their corner button; the next label offers the next number or letter. Save your own label presets (caption, colour and size), and they stay available across files.

ul.li: Label Exhibit Files (Tools menu): pick a set of PDFs, drag them into order, and label each on its first page with consecutive numbers, into copies named "Exhibit 3 - name.pdf" or in place.
Renumbering: run Label Exhibit Files again on labelled exhibits, in a new order, and the labels and file names all update together.

description.p: The menus are now behind a menu button at the right of the toolbar (or F10), leaving more room for pages; every keyboard shortcut works as before. Number boxes, such as the typewriter font size, keep their text off the left edge. Opening a document no longer shows a busy cursor over the window, which already says what it's opening.

Redaction, reworked. Mark exactly the words to remove, across line breaks, or draw a box around an area; marks show as a light wash, each with a button to remove it. Save Redacted Copy saves a separate "- Redacted" copy, in black, white or light grey boxes, and never changes the original.

ul.li: Bates Number Files: number a set of files in the order you choose, into copies that can be named by their first Bates number.
Find bar under the toolbar: searches as you type, with Match Case and Whole Words.
An OCR button that shows a red dot when a document has scanned pages without text, and a red dot on Save for unsaved changes.
Highlight selected text straight from the Highlight button, which now shows its colour as a stripe.
A collapsible page panel with centred thumbnails, lighter dialog icons, and a new app icon.
A PDF opened from the file manager goes to the window you used last and comes to the front, on X11 and on Wayland.

description.p: Faster start: the window appears straight away and says what it is opening, and opening a PDF while Kosmic PDF is already running is near instant. The busy cursor now shows from the moment of launch.
Icon: the Kosmos mark on its own, legible at panel size.
Icon: the Kosmos sparkle above "PDF" on a dog-eared page, in deeper colours.
New icon: the Kosmos mark above "PDF", in deeper colours.
Fixes the Flatpak failing to start.
Follows the desktop's dark mode even when its theme isn't available to the Flatpak.
